newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slip on late profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slip on late profit-taking.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGBs) futures subsided on profit-taking in late Tuesday trade but dealers said sentiment remained firm throughout the Japanese yield curve.
"Euroyen could break four to five ticks lower and still be within an uptrend," said a trader with a European futures house.
June Euroyen was unchanged against its IMM close at 99.36 at 1115 GMT. September was at 99.24 against 99.26.
Dealers said interest was increasingly shifting to the September contract as players continued to move down the yield curve in their search for value.
News that Japan's gross domestic product rose a real 0.1 percent in July-September from the previous quarter had little impact as the figure was within expectations.
"There was nothing in there which indicated the economy was growing stronger than previously believed," said the trader.
December JGBs settled at 126.62 against their previous 126.93 after opening at a new contract high of 127.00.
The trader said the JGBs came under pressure after a major bank unloaded a large amount of cash bonds in the market.

"There's talk of a 2 percent JGB yield but I can't see funds chasing yields down to 2 percent. It makes no sense," he said, adding however, that players remained reluctant to sell JGBs under current conditions.
A dealer with a U.S. institution said December JGBs could even head towards a target of 133.00 as players were beginning to speculate about an interest rate cut.
Eurodollar futures wavered within a two-tick range on a dearth of interest, but dealers said the market looked firmly underpinned following the recent bullish tone of U.S. bonds.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.53 against their IMM close at 94.54. June was at 94.46 against 94.47. Turnover for both months was less than 7,000 lots.
